bt-3qFe.title: Sign: red or blue town signs with town name
bt-3qFe.summary: Red or blue signs are common in towns and usually carry the name of the town you are in.

bt-6TGY.title: Landscape: flat land only in the south
bt-6TGY.summary: Flat landscapes like this only exist in the south, where coverage is limited to four regions.

bt-6ZzJ.title: Roadside: prayer flags
bt-6ZzJ.summary: Prayer flags near the road are typical here.

bt-FHkm.title: Landscape: wide flat valley, no big river
bt-FHkm.summary: A wide, fairly flat farming valley, the largest open valley with no major river visible on Street View.

bt-FySh.title: Plate: fully red plates
bt-FySh.summary: Licence plates are almost always red and easy to spot on vehicles. In Asia, no other country uses fully red plates.

bt-LdOA.title: Plate: yellow plate and roof on taxis
bt-LdOA.summary: Taxis have yellow plates and yellow roofs.

bt-M7LD.title: Pole: thin metal, black at the bottom
bt-M7LD.summary: Occasional thin metal poles, often painted black at the bottom.

bt-NdvV.title: Coverage: mostly main roads and cities
bt-NdvV.summary: Most coverage is on the main roads and in the cities.

bt-QdQ2.title: Airport: only one in the flat south
bt-QdQ2.summary: The only airport in the flat southern part of the country.

bt-RG1f.title: Coverage: late sunset lighting
bt-RG1f.summary: Late sunset coverage exists in two places: a small rural side road in the east, and a more urban area near a town in the west.

bt-TQCb.title: Airport: dry valley vs wet valley
bt-TQCb.summary: One airport is in a dry northwest valley, while the other, a domestic one, is in a wet northern valley.

bt-W6QG.title: Airport: in a dry northwest valley
bt-W6QG.summary: An airport sitting in a dry valley in the northwest, one of two northern airports.

bt-b3oU.title: Coverage: mountain roads, flat only in south
bt-b3oU.summary: Most coverage is on main mountain roads. Flat areas with no mountains only appear in the south.

bt-fJM0.title: Road marker: yellow top, white bottom
bt-fJM0.summary: Road markers have a yellow top and white bottom. On rural roads they are the best clue to your exact location, and on highways the road number is on top.

bt-iq4h.title: Language: Dzongkha script
bt-iq4h.summary: Dzongkha is an official language with unique-looking letters. On Street View these letters only appear here.

bt-s895.title: Google car: hook on the back
bt-s895.summary: A hook is visible on the back of the car in one western district, mainly in one town. It may be only barely visible through the blur.

bt-tkrk.title: Signpost: black-and-white stripes
bt-tkrk.summary: Signposts often have black and white stripes. Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Malaysia and Bangladesh have them too, so check other clues.

bt-uFJO.title: Guardrail: stone blocks along the road
bt-uFJO.summary: Stone blocks line winding rural roads instead of guardrails, which are rare. They are one of the best clues for rural roads here.

bt-uyf1.title: Houses: tin roofs, painted wooden frames
bt-uyf1.summary: Traditional houses have tin roofs and painted wooden frames, giving a very distinct look.

bt-y1Qr.title: Google car: grey, no antenna
bt-y1Qr.summary: A grey car with no antenna. It is the only left-hand-drive country with a grey car, but don't confuse it with a similar-looking white car.

bt-yGLe.title: Road lines: two solid white edge lines
bt-yGLe.summary: Two solid white lines on the outer edges only appear in the west, in the south and near the capital.
